 NEW UFC Qatar: Three Preliminary Fights to Watch Out For
 By Hank Strandberg 
 Edited by Drew Zuhosky Nov 20, 2026 7 hours ago 5 min read Follow on Google UFC Qatar brings a bevy of top-level mixed martial arts fights this weekend to the Middle East. 
 From This Article 1 . UFC Qatar Preliminary Fights: Amir Albazi vs. Alessandro Costa 
 2 . UFC Qatar Preliminary Fights:  Aleksandre Topuria vs. Santiago Luna 
 Bolstering the already impressive card are a collection of fun and entertaining preliminary matches that include pairings between ranked fighters looking to make their way up the ladder of their respective divisions. The undercard also will see a certain flyweight athlete seeking to compete for the second time in a calendar year since 2022 as he aims to remain relevant in the pecking order of his weight class. 
 These are three UFC Qatar preliminary fights to watch out for 
 UFC Qatar Preliminary Fights: Amir Albazi vs. Alessandro Costa 
 Back in 2022 at the then-UFC Apex in Las Vegas, Amir Albazi and Alessandro Costa faced off at UFC Vegas 66. Already three fights into his stint in the organization, Albazi stood as the more seasoned promotional fighter in comparison to Costa, who was making his UFC debut that night. Late into the third round, Albazi achieved a stunning uppercut knockout that ended Costa’s seven-bout winning streak. The finish also stood out as the first time the Brazilian had been beaten by strikes in six years.

 Ilia Topuria Reminds Aleksandre of Their Childhood Dreams 
 Nearly four years since their first pairing, Albazi and Costa will square off for a second time at UFC Qatar in a contest with much riding on the line for both men. 
 Once seen as a dominant figure in the talented flyweight category, Albazi has since been down on his luck after dropping two in a row to previous champion Brandon Moreno and Kyoji Horiguchi . Burdened by injuries that kept him outside the cage for well over a year, the Iraqi looked to be a step behind in his clash with the latter this past February. On a mission to not only earn his first win since June 2023, Albazi is wanting to make a statement this Saturday by closing the book on his rivalry with Costa and reasserting himself as a top contender at 125-lb. 
 Following his thrashing at the fists of Albazi, Costa has evolved into a stern prospect in the division. Going 5-2 in his last seven fights, “Nono” has bested several prominent flyweight combatants, including Matt Schnell and Cody Durden. While unfortunate losses to Steve Erceg and Alden Coria have kept the South American from reaching the title picture, a victory over the renowned Albazi will serve as the perfect fuel to rocket him into the weight classes upper echelon. 
 UFC Qatar Preliminary Fights:  Shamil Gaziev vs. Tallison Teixeira 
 In the heavyweight division, power reigns supreme, and at UFC Qatar, two of the literal biggest names in the sport will square off, as Russian power-puncher Shamil Gaziev taking on Brazilian phenom Tallison Teixeira. With a combined 17 knockouts between them, fight fans should expect the pair to throw some serious leather right from the get go. 
 Making his freshman Octagon outing in 2023 at UFC 296, Gaziev impressed in spades with a monumental performance over Martin Buday, toppling the Slovak with a second round knockout. The success of the finish, and his growing popularity with the fanbase earned the Russian main event honors in his next bout against African striker Jairzinho Rozenstruik , a fight that he would lose by fourth round technical knockout after being unable to answer the call for the final five minutes. 
 Once a towering figure in the 265-lb rankings, Gaziev has struggled to remain consistent over the past year, dropping two crucial matches to Waldo Cortes-Acosta and Brando Peričić. Getting back into the winner’s circle this past August with a thunderous starching of Kennedy Nzechukwu at UFC Fight Night 285, the Dagestan native is on the warpath to reclaim his spot in the top 15. 
 Beginning his professional career in 2021, Teixeira bulldozed his way through the competitive Brazilian regional circuit to secure a spot on season eight of the Contender Series. Backed by a 100% stoppage rate, with all of those coming in the first round, along with his absurd height of 6’8, he was pegged to easily dismantle his opponent, Arthur Lopes, which he did so with a sub two-minute starching. 
 Making his company debut five months later, the undefeated Teixeira made further waves by bringing down Justin Tafa in a mere 35 seconds. Sadly, “Xicão” has also encountered a great deal of difficulty with breaking through as a notable contender, as knockout losses to Derrick Lewis and Sergei Pavlovich have dropped the Brazilian’s stock considerably. 
 UFC Qatar Preliminary Fights:  Aleksandre Topuria vs. Santiago Luna 
 The older brother of acclaimed two-division champion Ilia Topuria , Alexsandre has begun to make a name for himself as a hot prospect in the UFC’s bantamweight category. Unbeaten in over a decade, the German-born fighter draws what looks to be his most deadly adversary yet in the young Santiago Luna. 
 Fighting solely in Spain for the first six contests, Topuria developed into a potent finisher, ending every single one of his victories before the final horn. Although he did end up losing a bout to Ivo Ivanov, he had rebounded amazingly by winning another three consecutive scrap following a six-year hiatus. 
 Getting the call to the promotion last year, Topuria went up against the unbelievably tough Colby Thicknesse at UFC 312, who was also making his debut. Dominating the Aussie throughout their three-round confrontation, the Georgian completely swept the scorecards, earning a trio of 30-27’s, along with the unanimous decision. Ending the year with another triumph, this time over Bekzat Almakhan, Topuria is seeking to make a case for a crack at the rankings when he faces Luna at UFC Qatar. 
 Something of an up-and-comer himself, Luna barreled into the UFC at Noche UFC 3 after an undefeated warpath built upon four submissions and two knockout wins. The Californian did not disappoint, flattening the prospective Quang Le in just two minutes. Defeating Angel Pacheco in his next time out, Luna would encounter the first real taste of adversity of his career when he locked horns with Ultimate Fighter alumni Bryce Mitchell, who choked him out with just eight seconds left in the fight.
